personas: Hispanic male in his 30s–40s living in the US West, single, agnostic, very liberal Democrat, living alone and working full-time with mid income and some college. Socially somewhat reserved but generally cooperative and warm; highly empathetic and environmentally minded, and wants to be seen as dependable, respected, and improving—though not necessarily loved by everyone. Emotionally reactive with elevated anxiety and stress sensitivity, preferring clarity and closure and often seeking the “best” option rather than settling, which can lead to worry or second-guessing. Not especially curious about abstract/novel ideas and tends to avoid heavy cognitive effort, yet can be logically reflective when prompted and is not prone to overconfidence. Financially tends toward impulsive spending and uses mental “buckets” for money; has only moderate comfort with numbers/financial concepts. In negotiations and sharing situations he aims to keep the majority while still maintaining a sense of fairness, is moderately trusting upfront, but less inclined to reciprocate generously once in the advantaged position.

Young Midwestern white woman in her 20s, an independent/moderate college student with mid income and a nonreligious lifestyle, who prefers simplicity and low clutter and likes to feel organized, in control, healthy, and “have life together.” Socially she’s fairly average in outgoingness but somewhat reserved and not especially warm/empathic; she cares about being liked and seen as kind, yet also wants status/admiration and to stand out. Decision-making tends to be careful and loss-averse: she’s very risk-avoidant, leans toward maximizing/optimizing, and prefers clear answers over ambiguity; she can think analytically when needed (good at suppressing gut mistakes, strong with numbers) but isn’t naturally drawn to deep intellectual exploration or novelty. With money and cooperation, she aims for fairness and avoids conflict—often generous in one-shot splits and willing to accept most deals—yet is cautious about trusting others upfront and keeps an eye on her own payoff; spending is somewhat impulsive compared to “tightwads.” Emotionally she’s generally steady with low depression/anxiety, but her self-concept is still forming, so she may seek structure, external validation, and concrete plans to stay on track.

Male in his 30s–40s living in the US South, never married, lives alone, works full-time on a low income; atheist, politically independent but socially/liberally oriented. Quiet, laid-back, and private, prefers small doses of social contact and can come off as cold despite not intending to; dislikes being the center of attention and would rather influence from behind the scenes. Extremely open-minded and creative (artist type), enjoys thinking through complex ideas, tolerates ambiguity, and tends to “good enough” decisions rather than exhaustive optimizing. Moderately emotionally reactive but not highly anxious; biggest self-identified friction is impatience with waiting, repetition, or perceived nonsense. Values autonomy and equality more than status or hierarchy, wants to be seen as fair, and often splits resources evenly; generally trusting and reciprocal, though can be tough in hard-bargaining situations. Strong preference for simplicity/minimalism and clear mental budgeting; financially cautious and risk-averse, not prone to impulsive spending, with average practical numeracy/financial knowledge.

Married, retired White woman in her 50s–60s living in the Northeast; conservative/Republican, culturally Protestant but not very observant, financially comfortable and highly financially literate. She’s moderately reserved and not strongly novelty-seeking, but enjoys thinking through complex issues and can be creatively associative; she’s more relationship- and fairness-oriented than status- or dominance-driven. Interpersonally she’s loyal and dependable, wants to keep promises, and often defaults to generous, “split it evenly” choices; she also tends to trust others and reciprocate fairness, but will reject deals she perceives as unfair. She can be bluntly judgmental and impatient with perceived incompetence, with some mild depressive/anxious tendencies, yet she’s not highly emotionally volatile. Decision-wise she’s practical and organized when she commits, but can be inconsistent with routine self-discipline; she’s relatively comfortable with ambiguity and doesn’t need quick closure, and she sometimes prefers standing out rather than blending in. She’s moderately pro-environment, not minimalist, and can be somewhat spendy/impulse-prone despite strong money knowledge.

White male (30–49) in the U.S. South, postgraduate-educated, single and living alone, employed full-time with mid income; politically moderate/independent and culturally Buddhist but non-practicing. Very introverted and low on novelty-seeking, preferring routine, simplicity, and a highly minimalist lifestyle; tends to be emotionally fairly steady with low anxiety but shows notable depressive tendencies. Interpersonally he’s polite and relationship-oriented yet somewhat reserved and not highly emotionally empathic; he values fairness and kindness and behaves generously and trusting in exchanges, while also caring about appearing socially appropriate. Cognitively he’s exceptionally strong at analytical reasoning, numeracy, and financial thinking, typically accurate about his own ability and comfortable with structured, rule-based decisions; he strongly prefers clear answers and closure over ambiguity. Motivationally he’s low on status/competitive drive and risk-taking, leaning toward security and balance; he aspires to be kind and wise, feels external pressure to be a high-performing academic scientist, but describes himself as calm, gentle, and prioritizing free time and personal life over career.

Young Hispanic man in the U.S. South, never married, Protestant but rarely attends, conservative/Republican, unemployed with moderate income and a 3-person household, and less than high-school education. He’s moderately social but not especially warm or cooperative—more competitive, blunt, and self-focused—while also emotionally reactive with noticeable mood swings and stress sensitivity. He values getting ahead and personal achievement more than harmony, wants to feel distinct, and isn’t highly concerned with appearing socially “correct.” Despite limited formal schooling and lower stored knowledge, he’s strong at on-the-spot logic, numeracy, and financial reasoning, and can think reflectively—though he doesn’t naturally enjoy deep, effortful thinking. Decision-wise he’s impatient and present-focused, tends to overspend and can be overconfident about his relative ability. In money-and-fairness situations he aims for “mostly fair” splits but typically keeps a slight edge for himself; he’ll extend moderate trust but expects reciprocity. He’s not particularly environmentally minded, is average on minimalism and empathy, and aspires to be more disciplined and reliable while trying to stay supportive to family without burdening others with his problems.

Married, high-earning West Coast woman in her 20s with postgraduate education; very liberal Democrat, agnostic, and strongly environmentally minded. Interpersonally warm, empathetic, cooperative, and fairness-focused—tends to be generous and trusting while also monitoring how she comes across and wanting to be seen as a good person. Highly conscientious and organized in day-to-day life, works hard and takes pride in contribution, but values downtime and balance; aspires to put others (future children) first without losing herself and feels trauma has reduced some spontaneity. Prefers clear answers and closure, often tries to optimize decisions, and leans toward minimalism rather than conspicuous uniqueness. Financially savvy and cautious: strong financial literacy, somewhat risk-averse, and a “tightwad” who dislikes spending; can be impatient about delayed rewards. Cognitively, she relies more on intuition than deep analytical deliberation, may overestimate her performance, and benefits from concrete options, simple comparisons, and external structure when making complex choices.

Young Southern U.S. woman (late teens–20s) with an associate’s degree, living with a partner in a small household, working full-time on a low income; politically moderate/independent and lightly religious. She is outgoing and socially confident but emotionally reactive and anxiety-prone, with a strong drive to keep relationships positive—highly empathetic, fairness-focused, and generally generous and trusting in social exchanges. She values both autonomy and group loyalty, wants to stand out (high need for uniqueness) yet is very attuned to how she comes across (high self-monitoring) and prefers clear answers and closure, often optimizing rather than “good enough” decisions. Curious and open to new ideas with strong on-the-spot problem-solving, but less anchored in accumulated factual knowledge; she’s moderately analytical and financially literate, uses clear mental “budgets,” and tends toward risk-averse choices. She’s motivated by improvement and responsibility—especially being a strong role model for her child—while recognizing personal growth needs around organization, time management, calmness, and emotional control.

Married Black Catholic woman in the Midwest (30–49), high-school educated, working full-time on a low income in a 3-person household; politically independent but conservative and highly involved in church. She is emotionally intense and easily stressed, with very high anxiety/depressive tendencies, strong sensitivity to threat, and a strong desire for certainty and clear answers; she can be critical and blunt, not naturally cooperative, and tends to trust others very little. Socially she’s more reserved than outgoing but can be loud/expressive when activated; she values being seen as kind, loving, productive, and respected, and feels strong “should” pressure to be selfless and always available. Cognitively she has solid reasoning/knowledge but prefers simple, practical information over effortful analysis; she wants closure, often maximizes, and is motivated by both self-advancement and maintaining relationships while also wanting to feel unique and not like everyone else. Financially she is highly risk-averse and very fairness/need focused: generous when terms feel fair but unwilling to give without control or obligation; she mentally budgets strictly, is impatient for near-term benefits, and is strongly shaped by immediate necessities rather than long-run ideals (including low interest in environmental causes).

Divorced white woman in her 50s–60s in the US West with an associate’s degree, unemployed, moderate income, atheist, and very liberal/Democrat. Socially outgoing, warm, and fairness-oriented; tends to share and cooperate, values equality, and is generally trusting while expecting equitable treatment. Curious and enjoys thinking through issues, but prefers clear answers and closure, often “maximizes” and second-guesses decisions; highly self-aware of how she comes across and adapts her behavior to social context. Low day-to-day structure and follow-through (struggles with motivation/consistency), and currently experiences high anxiety and depressive symptoms, with low confidence/clarity about who she is and how well she’s doing—leading to avoidance and worry about judgment. Financially and numerically average, somewhat impatient about delayed rewards, not minimalist (comfortable with more possessions/variety), moderately eco-leaning, and empathetic with a strong desire to leave things better than she found them.

Widowed Hispanic man in his 30s–40s living in the US South; self-employed, high-income, high-school educated, weekly religious attendee, and politically conservative/Republican. Socially he’s moderately outgoing but low on warmth/empathy and tends to be blunt or tough-minded; he cares about fairness and reputation and often chooses generous splits, especially when trust is involved. He’s highly risk-averse and prefers safe, predictable options, yet can be impatient about delayed rewards. Work style is inconsistent: he aspires to be organized and reliable, but in practice procrastinates, gets distracted, and follows through unevenly; he may benefit from structure and simple, actionable plans. Thinking style is more practical than intellectual—he doesn’t enjoy complex deliberation, relies on intuition, and overestimates his performance; he’s financially knowledgeable despite gaps in general knowledge/education. Emotionally he carries elevated anxiety and some depressive tone, with moderate self-certainty and low self-monitoring (less likely to adapt his presentation to others). Values lean agentic (self-advancement/independence) over communal bonding, with average interest in minimalism and a middling, not strongly ideological, pro-environment stance.

Midwestern white male (30–49), divorced, agnostic, politically moderate/independent, highly educated and high-earning, working full-time in a household of four. He is extremely conscientious, disciplined, and standards-driven—reliable, organized, and persistent—but also relatively low in warmth/agreeableness and empathy, so he can come across as blunt, impatient, or easily frustrated when others don’t meet expectations. More reserved than outgoing, emotionally steady with generally low anxiety, and moderately open to new ideas without seeking novelty for its own sake; he’s comfortable with ambiguity and tends to satisfice rather than obsess over “perfect” choices. Cognitively, he enjoys thinking through complex problems and shows strong reflective reasoning, numeracy, and financial literacy; he uses clear mental “budgets” and categories for money, is moderately risk-averse, and somewhat impatient about delayed rewards. Socially and economically he prioritizes fairness and reciprocity (often offering generous splits and returning fair amounts), though he may still manage impressions and present himself in a socially acceptable way. Values emphasize independence, hard work, trustworthiness, courage, and continual learning; he’s self-aware about needing more compassion and patience and actively tries to improve.

Married Black man in his 50s–early 60s living in the Western US, highly educated and high-income, working full-time and supporting a large household; Protestant who attends church occasionally and frames identity around being a faithful, loving, and financially responsible family leader. Socially confident, outgoing, cooperative, and highly disciplined/organized, with very low anxiety/depressive tendency and a clear, stable sense of self. Practical and tradition-leaning rather than novelty-seeking, prefers simplicity/minimalism, and likes clear answers and closure; adapts his presentation to context and is attentive to social norms (may answer in a socially desirable way). Strong quantitative/financial reasoning and reflective thinking; tends to be fair and reciprocity-minded—generous when giving and trusting, but unwilling to accept deals he deems unfair. Moderately pro-environment and politically moderate Democrat. Financial behavior can skew toward impulsive spending and impatience for delayed rewards, with otherwise average risk tolerance and relatively low sensitivity to losses.

Married Southern white woman (30–49), high-income and postgraduate educated, working full-time as a driven, detail-oriented CRNA; very conservative Republican and deeply involved in Protestant church life. Socially confident and assertive but not especially warm or naturally empathic; loyal to her in-group, values fairness and reciprocity, and is comfortable taking a leadership/mentor role. Highly conscientious, perfectionistic, and self-critical with some anxiety; strongly motivated by achievement and doing things “the right way,” prefers clear rules and certainty, and tends to over-optimize decisions rather than settle. Image- and context-aware (good self-monitoring) yet internally uncertain about identity, with a strong desire to stand out and a preference for minimalism. Numerically strong and practical, but less inclined toward abstract deliberation and can be overconfident in her judgments; money behavior skews tight/reluctant to spend despite comfort with strategic generosity and trust when reciprocity is expected. Environmentally minded and community-oriented, balancing ambition with duty, faith-based values, and a desire to make a meaningful positive impact.

Unemployed Hispanic woman in her 30s–40s in the Northeast, low income, high‑school educated, very liberal Democrat and nonreligious, living in a two‑person household. Quiet and socially withdrawn, not naturally cooperative or trusting at first, and low in drive for status or self-advancement; prefers autonomy and equality over group loyalty or hierarchy. Emotionally volatile with very high depression and elevated anxiety, prone to harsh self-criticism and feeling behind in life, yet strongly values being a “good person” who is patient and compassionate and wants genuine acceptance. Highly empathetic and fairness-minded in one‑off sharing situations, but cautious about giving others control and will keep more when trust is uncertain. Cognitively sharp (strong numeracy/financial literacy and quick reasoning) but doesn’t enjoy effortful thinking for its own sake; seeks clear answers and tends to maximize/optimize. Financially, tends toward impatience and very high risk aversion, with a spendthrift streak and mental “budgeting” habits; moderate interest in minimalism and only modest environmental orientation.

Married Hispanic man in his 50s–early 60s living in the Western U.S., high‑school educated, part‑time employed with a solid middle income; culturally Catholic but rarely attends, and strongly liberal/Democrat. He is outgoing, highly disciplined, competitive, and strongly achievement/status oriented, with a pronounced desire to stand out and a minimalist, no‑frills preference in lifestyle/choices. Interpersonally he can be blunt and low in warmth/empathy, prioritizing family above all but otherwise tending toward self-interest and skepticism about others’ motives; he may act “fair” in public or simple splits yet is unlikely to reciprocate trust when in control. Decision-making is pragmatic and optimization-minded with decent numeracy/financial savvy, moderate tolerance for ambiguity, and a tendency to rely on confidence and gut more than careful deliberation—often overestimating his own performance. He is notably risk-seeking and promotion-focused (drawn to upside and achievement), generally emotionally steady with low depression and average anxiety.

Midwest-based woman in her 50s–early 60s, college educated, Protestant and weekly churchgoer, politically independent but conservative, living in a two-person household with low income and currently unemployed. Highly outgoing, curious, and intellectually engaged—enjoys complex thinking, learning, and exploring options, and tends to “maximize” decisions rather than settle quickly; comfortable with ambiguity and may keep researching, which can create occasional indecision or feeling overwhelmed. Generally disciplined and reliability-oriented, with clear values and a desire to lead by example, though she can get distracted by too many competing tasks. Warm and prosocial with strong empathy and fairness norms: generous in sharing, inclined to trust and reciprocate, yet also willing to reject deals she perceives as unfair. Community- and relationship-focused with a strong sense of duty and loyalty, but not especially driven by status or personal dominance; prefers to fit in rather than stand out. Environmentally minded and numerate/analytical, but can be somewhat overconfident in her judgments and somewhat image-conscious in presenting herself positively. Financially, she’s more of a tightwad who dislikes spending, uses mental “budgets,” and is moderately patient about long-term tradeoffs; emotionally fairly steady with low anxiety/depressive tendencies.

Young Hispanic Catholic woman in the U.S. South (18–29), moderate Democrat, part-time worker with an associate’s degree, living in a 4-person household and is a mother; values family/community and shows strong empathy, fairness, and generosity, tending to share evenly and to trust others while also being somewhat cautious about being treated unfairly. Quiet and socially awkward/introverted but highly curious, creative, and open to new ideas; prefers collaboration and harmony over standing out, with low need to be unique and a generally grounded, honest response style. Emotionally tends to overthink and can be moderately sensitive to stress, yet reports low anxiety/depressive symptoms overall. Decision-making: enjoys thinking and exploring possibilities and is comfortable with ambiguity, but often relies on intuition and may struggle with complex logic, numbers, and especially financial concepts; benefits from clear, simple, step-by-step guidance and practical examples for money decisions. Spending is slightly tightwad-leaning and uses mental “budgets” to organize gains/losses; aspires to be more confident, well-spoken, successful, and—given parenting responsibilities—more patient, responsible, and selfless.

Married Hispanic Catholic woman (30–49) in the Western US with postgraduate education, a homemaker in a four-person household and moderate/independent politics. She is organized, tidy, and responsibility-driven, prioritizing family stability and fairness, and tends to be nurturing and patient with her children while more easily irritated with her spouse; she aspires to stay calm, logical, manage time better, and build financial independence. Socially she is middle-of-the-road (not strongly outgoing), somewhat pragmatic rather than novelty-seeking, and values both getting ahead and maintaining harmony, with strong loyalty to her in-group and respect for family roles. Decision-wise she thinks things through and likes optimizing choices, but can be overconfident in her judgments and may present herself in a socially acceptable light; she prefers clear, structured options and is risk-averse, cautious with spending, and motivated by practical benefits more than environmental or minimalist ideals.

Male in his 50s–60s, Asian, West US, self-employed with low income, never married, agnostic/nonreligious, very conservative Republican. Highly disciplined, organized, and detail-focused; prefers structure, clear rules, and decisive conclusions, and tends to optimize rather than “good enough.” Quiet and socially reserved, low on warmth/compassion, skeptical of others’ motives, and strongly self-reliant—expects people to act in self-interest and is unlikely to extend trust or generosity without proof. Pragmatic minimalist and tightwad who avoids waste, is highly risk-averse, and prefers predictable outcomes; financially and numerically savvy and capable of reflective, logical thinking, leaning on accumulated knowledge and experience. Emotionally steady with low anxiety/depressive tendencies, strong self-concept, low desire to fit in or stand out, and little interest in environmental or “virtue-signaling” causes; communicates bluntly and is comfortable being disliked while focusing on minding his own business.

Self-employed, high-income Asian American man in his 50s–60s living in the US South; postgraduate educated, divorced, nonreligious, politically moderate/independent, in a two-person household. He is calm, emotionally steady, and low in anxiety/depressive tendencies, with a kind, cooperative, fairness-oriented style that shows up in generous sharing and high interpersonal trust/reciprocity. Socially he’s more reserved than outgoing, not very concerned with standing out, and not highly image-managing; he tends to be genuine and consistent with a clear sense of self. Cognitively he’s very knowledgeable and verbally/logically strong, enjoys thinking through complex issues, and is comfortable with ambiguity (low need for closure), often satisficing rather than obsessively optimizing. He is disciplined and financially responsible with strong numeracy/financial savvy, uses mental “budgets,” and is moderately minimalist, yet he’s also relatively comfortable taking risks and is not especially loss-avoidant. Values emphasize relationships and family responsibility alongside independence, with strong pro-environmental preferences; he aims for a balanced life that supports family stability while leaving room for artistic and self-educational pursuits.

Young Asian American woman in the Western US (late teens/20s), college-educated, liberal/Democrat, atheist, currently unemployed and living in a large household. Socially she’s moderately outgoing but not especially accommodating, with a strong fairness/justice lens: she tends to give generously and trust others initially, yet can become punitive or “even-the-score” minded if she feels wronged. Emotionally she’s prone to anxiety, self-criticism, and overthinking/catastrophizing, with high personal standards that can make her judgmental of herself and others; she aspires to be braver, healthier, more optimistic, and to build a stable career while learning to prioritize self-care. In decisions she’s more of a satisficer than an optimizer, not strongly drawn to deep deliberation, and prefers practical, clear choices; she’s comfortable with some risk and not very loss-averse. She shows very strong on-the-spot problem-solving/novel reasoning and good financial literacy/numeracy, but is low on self-discipline/organization and follow-through, so she may start strongly yet struggle with routines and long-term execution. She’s not motivated by status or standing out, doesn’t tailor her self-presentation much, and isn’t especially minimalist or environmentally driven; spending control can be a weakness despite understanding money concepts.

Divorced, middle-aged white woman in the Northeast with postgraduate education but currently unemployed and on a low income, living alone; politically independent but conservative and nonreligious. She is calm and emotionally steady, moderately organized and cooperative, and somewhat reserved rather than highly outgoing. She thinks reflectively and can override snap judgments, but overall problem-solving/financial knowledge is only average, and she’s not a strong optimizer—she tends to satisfice and keep decisions simple. Interpersonally she is generous and highly trusting, motivated by fairness and “not being greedy,” yet she struggles to assert herself, is very concerned with appearing socially appropriate, and has low sensitivity to adjusting her presentation to situations; she describes herself as “too kind” and easily swayed, with a strong desire to be more self-reliant and stand up for herself. She is frugal/tight with spending, modestly minimalist, only mildly environmentally oriented, and has a noticeable desire to be distinctive while maintaining a clear, stable sense of who she is.

Young Asian American man in the Southern US, part-time employed with some college, moderate Democrat, loosely practicing Buddhist, living alone. Socially middle-of-the-road but tends to be blunt/low-warmth and low-empathy; will say yes to others yet is working on boundaries. Highly emotionally reactive and somewhat anxious, with a less stable self-image; craves certainty and quick resolution, and can be impatient with delayed rewards. Strongly self-advancing and status/achievement oriented, with a very high desire to stand out and a chameleon-like ability to manage impressions; motivated by self-improvement (especially fitness/attractiveness) but prone to procrastination and lower follow-through. Decision style is “optimize and be sure”: high maximization and need for closure, moderate enjoyment of deep thinking, and mixed reasoning skill (can handle structured verbal logic but struggles with reflective/abstract problem solving). Financially, tends toward spendthrift impulses and low financial literacy but uses mental “budgets”; moderately risk-tolerant and not very loss-averse. In bargaining is strategic and sometimes tough (generous when proposing but rejects many offers as a receiver), while in trust situations is surprisingly cooperative and strongly reciprocal—willing to give when trust is established, but not automatically generous without it.

Midwestern married white man (30–49) with an associate’s degree, high income, Protestant (attends monthly), politically independent but conservative. He’s dependable, hardworking, and highly conscientious, with a cooperative, fairness-oriented style; he values kindness, respect, trustworthiness, and doing what’s right, and tends to be generous in sharing decisions. Socially he’s more reserved than outgoing, prefers fitting in over standing out, and is not very image-managing or socially adaptive in the moment. He likes clear answers and closure, thinks problems through and enjoys effortful reasoning, and is financially/numerically savvy with a minimalist, somewhat tightwad spending style and structured “mental accounts.” He’s environmentally sympathetic despite conservative leanings. Decision-wise he can be impatient in the short term (present-focused) and somewhat overconfident about performance; he’s willing to trust others initially but may reciprocate less when roles reverse, and can be judgmental while wishing he were more empathetic. Emotionally, he experiences elevated anxiety and depressive symptoms despite generally steady outward behavior, and benefits from clarity, predictability, and supportive, respectful communication.

Black male in his 50s living in the US South, self-employed with some college, moderate income, never married, liberal/Democrat and nonreligious. Quiet and low-key socially (prefers small circles over lots of interaction) but notably warm, cooperative, and generally empathetic; tends to think in terms of fairness and others’ needs, yet is cautious about extending trust and may give more when reciprocity or social pressure is salient. Highly curious, idea-oriented, and drawn to novelty and distinctive choices; also prefers a minimalist lifestyle and wants to stand out rather than blend in. Decision style is analytical and financially savvy (strong money/number skills, structured “mental accounts”), but also perfectionistic—prone to maximizing, wanting clear answers, and overestimating how well he’ll do—so choices can become slow or stressful. Strong entrepreneurial/agency drive and desire for independence and upward success, motivated by providing for loved ones and helping his community; accepts hierarchy/authority when tied to group loyalty. Emotionally, he reports significant anxiety and depressive symptoms that can sap momentum and increase worry/rumination, even as he remains optimistic about being close to a breakthrough. Financially he’s a tight spender, somewhat impatient for near-term rewards, and relatively willing to take risks when the upside seems worth it.

Single, college-educated Jewish woman in her 50s living in the Western US, working full-time on a moderate income; politically conservative/Republican and not very environmentally oriented. She is highly curious, creative, and intellectually engaged, enjoys complex thinking, and tends to be decisive and uncomfortable with ambiguity; she also aims to optimize choices rather than “good enough,” and values being distinctive and original. Socially she is outgoing and can be an effective, patient teacher who wants to inspire and share beauty, but she is more self-directed than nurturing, with relatively low day-to-day empathy for people (stronger for animals/nature) and low baseline trust in strangers; in bargaining or giving contexts she is likely to keep resources unless fairness or clear reciprocity is established. She is extremely conscientious and self-controlled (prefers simplicity/minimalism), financially savvy, and willing to take risks, yet can be impatient for immediate outcomes. Emotionally she reports substantial anxiety and depressive tendencies, lower self-confidence and an uncertain self-concept, and can be loyal and forgiving in principle while holding long memories of past wrongs.

Young Black woman in the South, high-income household, student, moderate Democrat with low religious identification but weekly attendance; socially outgoing in comfortable settings yet shy about public speaking and wants to become more outspoken, optimistic, and high-achieving (straight-A, big-organization career, eventual business). Strongly self-advancing and status/achievement oriented, values standing out, and tends to compare favorably to others, but is less relationship/other-focused with notably low empathy and can be tough-minded. Emotionally, she experiences very high anxiety and has a less stable/clear self-concept, which can drive reassurance-seeking and second-guessing. Decision style: prefers simple thinking over deep analysis, but can do well on structured logic; struggles with numbers/quantitative reasoning and financial concepts, so benefits from concrete, step-by-step guidance. Financial behavior is mixed—high risk aversion and mental “budgeting,” yet also impulsive/spendthrift tendencies and strong impatience for delayed rewards. In fairness contexts she offers reasonably when negotiation is possible but is less generous when giving is purely voluntary; she is willing to trust initially but is less inclined to reciprocate.

Married, midlife Northeast U.S. woman with a college education, high income, and steady full-time work; moderate, independent, and weekly-practicing Catholic. She is organized, responsible, and follow-through oriented, but also emotionally sensitive—prone to anxiety, rumination, and self-criticism, with some jealousy/judgment she wants to outgrow and a desire to feel calmer and less concerned with others’ opinions. Socially she’s more reserved than outgoing, moderately warm and empathetic, and strongly fairness-minded and generous, tending to keep exchanges even and to trust others while reciprocating. She likes thinking through problems and learning from experience (strong practical/accumulated knowledge), yet can struggle with abstract logic/numerical details and shows some overconfidence in her performance. Decision-wise she’s more of a satisficer than an optimizer, prefers clear enough answers over endless deliberation, uses mental “buckets” for money, and is more spend-prone than tight—drawn to comfort/abundance rather than minimalism; environmentalism is not a primary motivator. She values achievement and doing well within hierarchies while also feeling strong loyalty and duty to her groups/family, and she’s motivated by avoiding mistakes and meeting responsibilities as much as by pursuing gains.

White married man in the Northeast, mid-career with a high-school education and solid middle income; liberal Democrat and atheist who rarely attends religious services. Quiet and reserved, more comfortable in small circles than social crowds, and generally warm, cooperative, and relationship-oriented, with a strong “family-first” ethic. Curious and open-minded, enjoys thinking through problems and can reason well when prompted, but day-to-day follow-through and organization are inconsistent; he tends to satisfice rather than optimize and is comfortable with ambiguity. Emotionally sensitive with elevated anxiety/depressive tendencies, low self-confidence/clarity about who he is, and difficulty regulating emotions; he aspires to be more confident and “have life figured out.” Very trusting and extremely generous in interpersonal/financial sharing situations, expecting mutual cooperation, yet can be surprisingly hard-nosed about fairness when given the chance to accept/reject deals. Financially cautious and reluctant to spend, uses strong mental “budgets,” but has only moderate comfort with numeracy/financial concepts. Low interest in standing out or managing impressions; tends to be candid rather than socially performative, and is not especially motivated by status or competition. Not particularly environmentally driven or minimalist in preferences.

Midwestern Asian-American married man in his 30s–40s with a college/postgrad background, high income, and moderate Democratic politics; socially confident and assertive, emotionally steady, and generally reliable/discipline-oriented, with a strong drive for achievement and efficiency. Pragmatic and routine-leaning rather than novelty-seeking, he prefers clear, workable solutions over exploring many options, and tends to satisfice. He thinks fairly analytically and can override gut reactions, is financially literate, and uses mental “budgets,” but is also somewhat impulsive with spending and biased toward immediate rewards. Interpersonally he’s not highly image-managing or socially adaptive—more direct and consistent across settings—showing average empathy but a self-interested bargaining style: willing to trust somewhat yet inclined to keep resources and return less unless compelled, while still wanting to be seen as responsible and principled. He aspires to continuous growth, integrity, and balancing ambition with kindness, but can become impatient when things feel inefficient.

Middle-aged Black man in the U.S. South, living alone and working full-time on a modest income; socially reserved and low on novelty-seeking, preferring familiar routines and practical, no-frills choices. Extremely conscientious, organized, and reliable, with very low anxiety/depressive tendency and a clear, stable sense of identity; tends to want closure and make deliberate, “best-choice” decisions rather than winging it. Not especially expressive or emotionally empathetic, but strongly fairness-minded and considerate in resource-splitting, while also careful not to disadvantage himself; generally cautious about trusting others with money and expects balance/reciprocity. Thinks clearly under pressure and can override gut impulses, with solid numeracy/financial basics; may dislike long, abstract intellectual deep-dives but handles concrete problem-solving well.
